checkpoints: After an edit is accepted for an open document, the latest text is pending in that document's store-owned trailing task and has not yet been written by that edit.
At the end of 120 ms without another edit for the same document, the trailing callback writes the latest pending text exactly once.
After a trailing callback completes, the task is reusable: a later edit burst can schedule and complete another save.
Closing, disposing, or navigating away detaches the view badge but does not discard an already pending document-buffer save.
Search-preview queries retain their separate 40 ms trailing behavior, and hide still cancels only the preview task.
forbidden_effects: Do not write each accepted edit directly to the environment/store on every keystroke.
Do not cancel or destroy a document's pending BufferBank task when its Badge is detached, the document is closed, or another document is opened.
Do not move document-buffer ownership into Badge or otherwise tie buffer lifetime to the current view.
Do not change Preview query/hide behavior or its 40 ms quiet interval.
Do not change the public workspace, preview, environment, store, output, source-identity, text, status-payload, or document-payload interfaces and semantics beyond edit-write timing and coalescing.
Do not let a synchronous save listener corrupt, repeat, redirect, or cancel the save that invoked it.
lifecycle_identity: There is one reusable Trailing document buffer per document id in Store.bufferBank.entries, obtained through BufferBank.get(env,id).
Opening the same document id reuses its existing store-owned trailing buffer rather than creating a Badge-owned replacement.
Badge remains a live subscription for the current view only; detaching it removes that subscription without ending the document buffer.
Workspace close/dispose advances the workspace generation and retires the current Badge, while document-buffer lifetime remains independent.
Preview owns a distinct Trailing instance and is not part of the document BufferBank.

obligations.text: Workspace.edit(text), when a document is current, must enqueue the text through that document's existing BufferBank Trailing task rather than call env.write immediately.
Document edits must use the existing 120 ms trailing delay; each new edit in the same pre-flush burst replaces the pending text and resets the scheduled callback so only the latest text is written.
When the 120 ms quiet interval completes, the document task must call env.write with the original document id and the latest pending text exactly once for that burst.
After one burst flushes, the same per-document task must remain able to schedule and save subsequent bursts.
Pending document saves must survive view retirement, close, dispose, and navigation because the BufferBank—not Badge—owns them.

Before invoking the callback-capable env.write boundary, Trailing.flush must retain its existing transition to an idle state by clearing its handle and pending value, preserving correct behavior if a synchronous store listener navigates or initiates more work.

All non-edit behavior and public interfaces must be preserved, including document/status output payloads, subscription behavior, source ids/text, open/close/dispose behavior, and synchronous store notification semantics.
Preview must remain unchanged, including its independently owned 40 ms trailing task and hide-time cancellation.

ordering_barriers: For a document burst, cancel the prior scheduled handle before scheduling the replacement 120 ms callback.
A scheduled flush must capture the pending latest text and clear handle/pending state before invoking env.write, because env.write can synchronously reach store listeners and navigation.
Workspace retirement must detach the old Badge and emit the existing document-null output without canceling the store-owned document task.
A document's delayed write remains associated with the id captured when its BufferBank entry was created, even if another document is current when the callback runs.
Store.write must retain its existing order: update records, construct the event and increment revision, then synchronously notify a snapshot of listeners.
preservation: Preserve createWorkspace operations open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose(), and createSearchPreview operations query(text) and hide().
Preserve the existing document retirement/open output sequence and payload construction.
Preserve Badge's id-filtered status subscription and its detachment when the view retires.
Preserve synchronous Store read/write/subscribe behavior and listener notification semantics.
Preserve all original document ids, text values, revision/status payloads, and output kinds.
Preserve Preview as a transient, independent feature with its current quiet interval and cancellation behavior.
scope: Change only document-edit persistence timing in src/Workflow.java: coalesce Workspace.edit calls with the existing per-document Trailing task using a 120 ms quiet interval.
Use Store.bufferBank as the owner of persistent document buffers.
Workspace open/close/dispose, Badge subscriptions, Store behavior, output payloads, and Preview are preservation scope, not redesign scope.

Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet
interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts
must continue to save.
Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces.
The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

Railway operations — A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate. Preview is transient and owns a different quiet interval. Document-buffer responsibility: store-owned BufferBank

createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide(). Store read/write/subscribe is synchronous; timer schedule(callback,delay), cancel(handle) is explicitly controlled. Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription. A store listener may call navigation synchronously. All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics.
void push(String text) { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); pending=text; handle=env.schedule(this::flush,delay); }
void flush() { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); String text=pending; handle=null;pending=null; if(text!=null)work.accept(text); }

static final class BufferBank {final Map<String,Trailing> entries=new HashMap<>();Trailing get(Environment env,String id){return entries.computeIfAbsent(id,k->new Trailing(env,120,text->env.write(k,text)));}}
void edit(String text){Badge view=current;if(view!=null){env.write(view.id,text);}}

static final class Preview {final Trailing task;Preview(Environment env){task=new Trailing(env,40,q->{Map<String,Object>v=new LinkedHashMap<>();v.put("query",q);env.output("preview",v);});}void query(String text){task.push(text);}void hide(){task.cancel();}}

triggers: Calling Workspace.edit(text) while current is non-null pushes text into the current document's BufferBank task.
Another edit for the same document before its scheduled callback fires cancels/replaces that schedule and pending text.
Expiration of 120 ms with no replacement edit invokes the document task's flush.
A later edit after a completed flush starts a new independent burst.
Opening, closing, disposing, or synchronously navigating may change the current Badge but must not cancel an already scheduled store-owned document flush.
unknowns: The public sources do not specify scheduler behavior for callbacks that become due at exactly the same instant as a new edit; preserve the Environment scheduler's ordering rather than inventing a tie-break rule.
The public sources do not specify cross-document ordering when multiple document buffers become due; each buffer must retain its own id, text, and 120 ms trailing semantics.
The concrete Environment.write implementation is not shown; the contract relies on the documented synchronous store/listener boundary and the existing BufferBank callback to env.write.
The public sources do not define error handling if schedule, cancel, env.write, output, or a listener throws; no new exception policy should be inferred.
No explicit requirement states that opening a document must display unsaved pending text before its delayed write; preserve the existing open behavior, which reads from Store records.
